newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes mostly up on CBOT soy surge.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes mostly up on CBOT soy surge.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed mostly higher, boosted by renewed strength in CBOT soybeans and Japanese demand, floor sources said.

They noted a stronger yen versus the Canadian dollar appeared to have sparked interest from Japan with futures buying Tuesday expected to be followed by overnight purchases of Canadian canola in the export market.

The recent decline in crush margins, however, limited buying interest from domestic crushers. Hedge selling in new crop months was also a feature with a large acreage expected to be planted this year after recent price strength.
May canola closed $6.00 higher at $429.20. Flaxseed was also mostly higher with May up $1.50 at $356.50.
Feed wheat prices were lower on commercial selling and weak CBOT corn with May off $1.10 at $172.00. Western barley was also down on commercial selling. May fell $1.10 to $141.60.
July feed peas ended down US$1.50 at $188.50 after earlier dipping to a contract low of $188.00.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
